Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the throughput looked promising. We're lining up an early Dedicated pilot (production-similar traffic) and need a pragmatic SKU recommendation for the first 90 days. High level:
- Workload: mixed chat (long-context, 16k tokens tail in some sessions) + dense vector embeddings for retrieval (batch and on-demand).
- Peak: ~75 concurrent chat sessions (~2–4 requests/sec per session during spikes) + embedding bursts of ~600 qps for short windows.

- Budget: narrow — procurement prefers not to over-commit but will consider reserved capacity if clearly justified.

Specific ask: H100 vs A100 vs L4 — memory vs throughput tradeoffs, how to mix for predictable latency with cost control, and recommended reserved vs burst split. If you can include a rough VM/GPU count for the above peak and a fallback plan if capacity is hit, that would be very helpful.

Hi all — technical breakdown below (keeps to the specific H100 / A100 / L4 tradeoffs requested). I'll summarize at the top, followed by numbers and assumptions.

TL;DR recommendation: hybrid pool — small H100-backed pinned fleet for long-context chat state (KV-heavy, memory-bound), A100 nodes for steady midweight chat and model variants, and L4 as low-cost ephemeral burst capacity for short-context generation and embedding-only loads. Reserve H100 for the smallest set of sessions that require 16k context; rely on fallback quantized 70B -> 13B policy for non-critical sessions.

Assumptions:
- Model candidates: 70B (quant 4-bit) ~ needs ~40–60GB effective working memory including KV cache for 16k; 13B ~ 16–24GB. Embedding model: 2–7GB working set per request (depending on batch).
- Network + batching: we use request-level batching for embeddings (highly efficient) and continuous small batching for chat.
- Latency targets: 95p chat <350ms for short responses; long-context stream has higher jitter tolerance.

Hardware notes:
- H100 80GB: best for memory-dense long-context runs — allows a single replica to host larger KV caches and run 70B quant with reasonable throughput. Good for stateful conversational replicas.
- A100 80GB: strong balanced throughput, cheaper than H100 for sustained throughput, slightly less performance on large attention kernels. Good for 13B/34B steady chat and higher-concurrency embedding batching when memory fits.
- L4 24GB equiv: much cheaper, lower-memory. Great for embeddings and short-context generation; struggles with 70B/long-context without aggressive offloading/quantization. Excellent for bursty embedding QPS due to cost and fast cold-start behavior.

Sizing math (rough, for planning):
- Chat long-context demand: assume 75 concurrent sessions, of which ~20% will require long-context (16k) at any spike => 15 long-context sessions. Each H100-backed replica can sustain ~6 long-context interactive sessions at desired latencies (bound by KV and attention kernels) => need 3 H100 replicas pinned.
- Chat midweight demand: remaining chat sessions (60 sessions) using 13B/34B variants. An A100 replica can handle ~12 concurrent midweight sessions => need 5 A100 replicas for steady headroom.
- Embedding bursts: peak 600 qps for short windows. Embedding batching: with batching and L4 throughput, one L4 can handle ~200-300 qps embedding (batched) depending on batch shaping. Plan for 3 L4 replicas for burst capacity (can be ephemeral, auto-scale).
- Network/throughput buffer: add 20% headroom across pools for autoscaling thresholds.

Reserve vs burst guidance:
- Reserve: pin 3x H100 and 3x A100 for baseline SLA-critical traffic (ensures long-context and steady chat coverage).
- Burst (ephemeral): additional 2–3 A100 and 3–6 L4 for burst/embedding windows. Use rapid scaling policies and fallback routing (if H100 saturated, route to A100+quantized model with elevated latency guardrail).

Fallback policies and graceful degradation:
- If long-context H100 pool saturates, immediately route new long-context sessions to a quantized 70B with reduced KV (higher latency) or to 13B with a short-context fallback and a user prompt indicating degraded context.
- Maintain prefix-KV cache for returning sessions on H100 to reduce rebuild cost.

Ops notes:
- Monitoring: set token-level and KV-cache hit metrics; track 95p latency per model variant and per pool.
- Cost control: prefer L4 for embedding-heavy periods; strongly gate H100 use to sessions that truly need 16k context.

I'll attach a quick worksheet with the per-GPU throughput numbers used here. Happy to run tighter sims if you share a representative sample of session lengths and embedding batch distributions.

— Dev
Dev Patel
Senior Inference Engineer, Redwood Inference

Lina / team — building on Dev's numbers, here's a 90-day allocation sketch with operational considerations and a simple cost/comms framing for Procurement.

90-day pilot allocation (initial reserved + burst):
- Reserved pool (month-to-month reservation recommended for initial predictability):
  - 3 x H100-80GB (pinned) — covers long-context steady sessions and reduces cold KV rebuilds.
  - 3 x A100-80GB (pinned) — baseline midweight chat throughput and backup for long-context overflow.
- Burst / autoscale pool (on-demand, pay-as-you-go):
  - up to 3 additional A100s for HQ bursts (warm start via container snapshotting).
  - up to 4 L4 GPUs for embedding bursts and cheap short-context fallthroughs.

Operational rationale:
- Start conservative on H100 count (3) to keep committed spend down but ensure user experience for long-context. If KPIs show higher long-context concurrency, move +1 H100 at 30-day review.
- Use A100s as the workhorse for steady traffic — cheaper than H100 while handling a lot of medium-context loads.
- L4s are the scaling lever for embedding density and sudden burst cost control. Keep these ephemeral and tightly monitored.

Estimated monthly commit vs peak delta (illustrative):
- Committed (3H100 + 3A100): estimated baseline token-hours cost X (we can provide a line-item).
- Peak (with burst pools): add 3A100 + 4L4 on-demand incremental cost ~ +40–60% relative to commit during peak windows.

SOW / procurement notes to include:
- SLA targets: baseline 99.5% availability for reserved pools; we recommend a short escalation clause for any capacity shortfall during first 90 days.
- Rollout cadence: week 0–2 deploy reserved fleet and test with production traffic shadowing; week 3–6 open bursts to live traffic and measure cost/latency; week 8–12 calibrate reservation count.
- Acceptance criteria: 95p chat latency below 350ms for baseline flows; embedding p95 throughput >= 80% of peak target when burst pools active.

Next steps: we can push a draft SOW and an estimated month-by-month cost table Monday afternoon. Procurement — if you can confirm preferred billing term (monthly vs quarterly commit) and any vendor compliance fields we should populate (SOC2, IP requirements), we'll fold that in.

Thanks — will prepare the SOW and an ops-runbook snippet you can drop into your onboarding docs.

— Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
